plugin.name: Jujutsu VCS Integration
plugin.description:
Native IntelliJ integration for Jujutsu (jj), a Git-compatible version control system with a fundamentally different approach to working with code.

Why Jujutsu?

Jujutsu treats your working copy as a commit—always. No staging area, no "dirty" state. Just describe what you're working on and keep coding.

Key Features

  • Describe-First Workflow — Working Copy tool window for describing current work and creating new changes.
  • Custom Log View — Visual commit graph with inline change IDs, descriptions, and bookmarks.
  • Change Operations — Edit, abandon, and describe changes directly from the log.
  • File History & Annotations — Full file history with diff viewer and line-by-line blame.
  • Multi-Repository Support — Work with multiple JJ repositories in a single project.
  • Real-Time Status — Auto-refresh keeps the UI in sync as you edit files.

GitHub · Issues
plugin.change-notes:
0.9.2

Added

  • **Inline hunk checkboxes in Split and Squash Into…**: the file preview now shows the file's full change with a checkbox in the gutter of every hunk. Tick the hunks that should move to the new commit (or into the destination) directly, without opening **Pick Hunks…**. The file's checkbox in the list goes half-checked for a partial selection, and a summary under the file name says how many hunks move. **Pick Hunks…** is still there for line-level edits. ([#101](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/101))
  • **Squash preview**: the Squash Into… dialogs (Squash Into…, Squash Into Here from…, Squash into Parent…) now show the log graph as it will look after the squash. The destination is highlighted, and the source row disappears (or stays, if it will keep a remainder or you keep emptied sources), with its children re-parented, so you can see the result before clicking OK.
  • **Abandon Changes**: select several changes in the log and abandon them together from the right-click menu. It is available when every selected change is mutable and in the same repository, runs as a single operation (one Undo restores all of them), and asks once, summarising what would be lost, including any local bookmarks that will be deleted. Selecting 10 or more changes always asks first.
  • **Drop Changes from This…**: right-click one or more files in a mutable historical commit's changed-files list (or the editor for a file opened at that revision) to remove their changes from that commit, resetting them to their content in its parent. Descendants are rebased, and it runs as one operation (one Undo). It is disabled while several commits are selected. ([#148](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/148))
  • **Revset search**: a new toggle beside Regex / Match Case / Words in the log's search box treats what you type as a jj revset instead of text to match, ANDed with the tab's scope and the other filters. A revset jj rejects outlines the box in red with a short message about just that text in its tooltip, and the log keeps its previous rows. When the toolbar is too narrow to leave room to type, the search box now collapses to a compact chip that pops the full box out. The setting is remembered per tab. The commit-picker dialogs and file history don't have it. ([#116](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/116))
  • **Revset highlighting, completion and history**: every place you type a revset (the Scope popup, the search box in revset mode, the Log revset and Diff Base revset in Settings including per-repository overrides, and Set Diff Base → Custom revset…) is now an editor-style field. It colours functions, strings, operators and parentheses; completes jj's functions, your bookmarks and tags, and your revset aliases (accepting a function puts the caret inside its parentheses); and underlines the exact character where jj reports a syntax error. Settings' **Test** button now also outlines the field and shows a short one-line error instead of jj's raw output. A history drop-down on the Scope popup and the search box keeps your last five revsets, including those from before this change (a scope saved as an alias counts too), followed by a **Saved aliases** section listing your jj revset aliases (repository ones marked) so you can pick one by name. The search box's history also remembers the Regex, Match Case, Words and Revset switches each search was run with, shows them beside the entry, and restores them when you pick it. ([#116](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/116))
  • **Save a revset as a jj alias**: the Scope popup has a **Save as alias…** link, and the search box a button when in revset mode, that save the revset you typed as a jj revset alias in your user config (or each repository's config). After saving, the box or scope switches to the alias name, so it also works in the `jj` command line and follows later edits to the alias. It asks before overwriting an existing alias. ([#116](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/116))
  • **Filtered log graph joins visible commits across hidden ones**: when a filter or revset hides commits in between, each visible commit is now connected to its nearest visible ancestor by a wavy line, the way `jj log` shows elided revisions, instead of being left as an unrelated row. A commit with no visible ancestor still ends in a short wiggly stub. Hovering the line says "Revisions hidden by the current filter", and clicking it jumps to the ancestor. ([#131](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/131))

    • Changed

  • The log's **Revset** filter is now the tab's **Scope**. It sits at the left of the toolbar, before the search box, and the search and the other filters narrow within it. It never collapses into the overflow menu, and clearing filters keeps it. Navigating to a change outside the scope offers to clear it, and the scope is shown as code with a link to jj's revset documentation. Revset filters you saved carry over as each tab's scope. ([#116](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/116))
  • The log's **search box now pops out** into a wide popup when you click into it, in text mode and revset mode alike, so a long search or revset has room to be read; it returns to its place when you click away or press Esc. The commit-picker dialogs and file history keep their plain box.
  • **Log filters now search the whole history.** Search text, the Reference, Author and Date filters and the Revset filter are resolved by jj, a page at a time, instead of only filtering the commits already loaded. A search or revset matching old commits shows them without pressing Enter (the table holds its previous rows and shows "Filtering…" while jj answers), and scrolling loads more matches. The Reference filter now shows the bookmark or tag's complete ancestry rather than just the part that was loaded, and the "matches outside the loaded window" notice is gone. ([#116](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/116))
  • **Faster log refresh on large repositories**: after New Change, Commit, or abandoning an empty working copy, the log graph is re-laid out only where it changed instead of for every loaded row, so the refresh no longer slows down as you scroll deeper into history. Loading the log for the first time is also quicker, since the graph is now laid out once rather than twice.

    • Fixed

  • Typing a half-formed revset in the log's search box no longer writes a warning to the IDE log for every keystroke.
  • A **stale workspace** (changed by another workspace or jj command) no longer causes an "Uncaught exception in background task" error when the IDE starts or the log refreshes. The log now shows the usual "Update stale workspace" notification, once, and recovers after you click it. Previously the log tab was left empty with only a log-file warning.
  • Revset errors in the Scope popup and **Save as alias…** are now readable: the popup shows jj's explanation and column in a wrapping error balloon instead of a truncated line (including for errors inside an alias), and **Save as alias…** refuses an invalid revset without writing it, keeping the Revset field editable so you can fix it in place. ([#116](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/116))
  • Scrolling deep into a very large repository's log is much smoother. The log now loads bigger pages the further you scroll, sized so each fetch takes about 0.7 s (a slower machine or a wider graph gets smaller pages, up to 8,000 rows at most), and pages that arrive close together are applied to the table once instead of one by one. On an 86,000-commit repository a full load now takes 13 page fetches instead of 44, with about a third of the table-update and graph-layout work.
  • In a large paged log, clicking the faded line below a change loads its parent and now keeps it in view. Previously the rows that filled in between could push the new selection off-screen.
  • Searching the log (or a picker) for a short text such as a single letter no longer fails with "Change ID prefix is ambiguous".
  • The log's hover tooltip no longer appears instantly in Rider. It now waits for the same delay as the IDE's standard tooltips (`ide.tooltip.initialReshowDelay`, 500 ms by default), which also means it shows after 500 ms rather than 1.2 s in IntelliJ IDEA. ([#144](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/144))
  • Cancelling **Retrieving annotations**, a log load, file history or another background jj read now stops the jj process straight away. Previously it kept running until it finished or timed out (up to two minutes for annotate), so on slow repositories abandoned jj processes could pile up. Commands that change the repository still always run to completion. A command that changes the repository and was started just as a background task was cancelled is no longer reported as timed out after 30 seconds when it actually succeeded. ([#64](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/64))
  • The Restore dialog's "N files will be restored" line no longer reads "0 files" until you toggle a checkbox when files are pre-selected.
  • **Comparing with a commit that has since been rewritten** now compares against that exact commit. Compare with Another Commit… (on a commit, or on a file from history), Compare Before with Another Commit… and Pin to Revision… used to resolve a typed commit id to the change's current version, so the comparison showed the working copy against itself. The revision picker also shows each commit's id and marks rewritten (hidden) commits. ([#130](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/130))
  • **Diffs, file history, annotate and the diff base now read the exact commit you selected.** A rewritten (hidden) commit shares its change id with the visible one, so these used to silently show the current version's content. If a commit can no longer be found, you now get "Commit … is no longer available" instead of a raw jj error. ([#130](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/130))
  • **A remote bookmark left at a rewritten (hidden) commit** (for example after you amend a pushed change locally) is now shown as that commit. The bookmarks panel tooltip shows the old commit instead of the working copy, the ahead/behind counts are measured against it, the revision picker labels it by commit id, and New Change, Edit, Rebase and Duplicate are no longer offered on that row, since they would have acted on the current version. Navigate Log to Bookmark is disabled for it. ([#130](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/130))
  • **A change that becomes divergent between viewing it and acting on it** (Describe, Edit, Abandon, Split, Squash…) now shows "Change … has become divergent" and refreshes the log, instead of a raw jj error. The action is never retried automatically. ([#130](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/130))
  • The Rebase, Squash Into… and Duplicate Onto… dialogs no longer freeze for minutes on large repositories (thousands of loaded commits), including when switching between revision/source/branch modes or typing in the search box. ([#149](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/149))
  • **Advance Bookmark** now respects your `revsets.bookmark-advance-to` jj setting instead of always moving the bookmark to the working copy. ([#146](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/146))
  • Jujutsu menu actions (history, restore, compare, squash, split, diff) are now disabled for files that are ignored and not tracked, since jj has nothing to offer for them; **Annotate** is hidden. Tick **Tracked** to bring such a file under jj, and tracked-but-ignored files are unaffected.
  • Editing an immutable working copy (`jj edit --ignore-immutable`) no longer leaves you confused when your edits end up in a new change on top. That is jj's own protection, applied by any command that snapshots, including the plugin's background refreshes. The plugin now says so in a notification, and **Squash into Immutable Commit...** (also on the child's right-click menu) folds the edits back into the immutable commit after confirmation. ([#143](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/143))
  • **Change actions on far-back bookmarks and tags**: New Change, Edit, Rebase and Duplicate are now offered on a bookmarks-panel row whose change is outside the log's loaded window. They used to be missing from the menu. The row's change is fetched when you select it, so the menu may open a moment late.
  • Opening a file no longer shows a "nothing to annotate" balloon when annotations are preloaded in the background for a file that did not exist at the configured diff base.

    • See full release notes for details.
